Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking our call earlier. As we evaluate Redwood for a Europe-first deployment of our patient-facing assistant, our legal and privacy teams have compiled a short technical & policy questionnaire focused on transfer neutrality and localization options. We need concise, attributable answers for procurement and our Data Protection Officer.

High-level asks:
- Confirm whether customer data can be restricted to EU-resident processing only (including inference, logging, backups).
- Describe routing policies (how requests are routed by region and model variant), and whether routing is auditable per-tenant.
- Explain legal transfer mechanisms you support between EU and non-EU zones (SCCs, DPF/SCC combo, standard contractual clauses + supplementary measures, or on-prem offering).
- Provide an export-control / sanctions screening note (do you filter or block requests with embargoed destinations?).
- Clarify encryption & key management: per-customer keys, BYOK, HSM/KMS options, and zero-access support for the control plane.
- Detail retention and deletion semantics for request logs, KV caches, and model telemetry.
- List of subprocessors (only if you can provide a current snapshot) or a pointer to the latest matrix.

We appreciate short, numbered answers and any attached artifacts (proof of SOC2/ISO, DPA template, subprocessor matrix). Can you respond by EOD Friday (2028-07-28)?

Thanks — we want to move this to procurement shortlist next week.

Best,
Elena Sokolov
Head of Security & Privacy
MedBridge Health

Elena — thanks for the request. Below are concise, attributable answers to your numbered bullets; where helpful I’ve indicated the artifact name (attached) or a link.

1) EU-only processing capability
- Short answer: Yes. For customers requiring EU-resident processing, we support three deployment modes: Hosted (EU regions only, with regional routing and regional model variants), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools in EU datacenters), and Private (VPC/on‑prem package for full data residency).
- Evidence: Redwood_Transfer-Neutrality_Summary_20280725.pdf (section A) and subprocessor_matrix_20280725.csv.

2) Routing policies and auditability
- Requests can be routed by policy: region, latency, cost tier, or customer-specific pinning. We provide per-request routing metadata (region, model_variant, instance_id) logged to the customer’s audit stream and retained per their retention policy.
- Auditability: Logs include route decisions and fallback events; these are queryable via the Console and can be exported via log export APIs.

3) Legal transfer mechanisms supported
- We support SCCs and have a DPA Annex that describes cross-border safeguards. For US–EU transfers we support the Data Protection Framework (DPF) where customers rely on it; we also offer on‑premise packages and Dedicated EU-only capacity for avoidance of cross‑border transfers.
- For higher-assurance customers, we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments.

4) Export-control / sanctions screening
- We do not perform content-level sanction screening by default. Customers with sanctions screening obligations can enable an add-on that performs outbound destination checks and blocks payloads flagged by configured rules. We can also integrate with third-party screening vendors on Dedicated/Private deployments.

5) Encryption & key management
- In transit: TLS 1.2+ and mTLS for inter-service traffic.
- At rest: AES-256 encryption for caches and persisted logs.
- KMS options: Managed KMS (Redwood-managed), customer-managed KMS in cloud (BYOK), and on-prem HSM for Private installs.
- Zero-access: For BYOK configurations we use envelope encryption so that Redwood cannot decrypt customer dataset keys without the customer’s KMS credentials.

6) Retention & deletion semantics
- Request payloads: default retention 30 days (configurable per account; options 7/30/90/365 or custom on Enterprise plans).
- KV cache: configurable TTL per application; customers can clear KV caches via API.
- Logs & traces: retention configurable; we support legal‑hold and export prior to deletion.
- Deletion: we provide documented API endpoints for data deletion and a formal erasure certificate on request.

7) Subprocessors
- Attached: subprocessor_matrix_20280725.csv (current snapshot). The matrix lists infra providers by region, backup storage vendors, monitoring, and CDN partners. We update the published list monthly; customers are notified for critical changes.

Additional notes:
- Model & variant localization: We offer EU-only model variants (quantized versions hosted in EU) to minimize export risk; automatic fallbacks to non-EU variants are opt-in and can be disabled for a tenant.
- Data minimization & pseudonymization: We support pre-processing hooks in the SDK for tokenization/pseudonymization before sending data to Redwood, plus masking rules in the Console for logs.
- Audits: SOC2 Type II is available under NDA; ISO 27001 is in progress.

Attachments included in this email: subprocessor_matrix_20280725.csv (subprocessor snapshot), Redwood_Transfer-Neutrality_Summary_20280725.pdf (one-page answers). Also linking the DPA template here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cRedwoodTransferSummary

If you’d like, we can prepare a short one-page addendum that maps each questionnaire item to contractual DPA language for procurement. Suggest a 30-min follow-up Tuesday morning next week to walk through any high-risk items.
